PRESIDENT'S ORDER 14 of 1979
PRESIDENT'S ORDER 14 of 1979
NATIONAL AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES (BASIS OF ELECTIONS) ORDER, 1979
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 13th September, 1979]
No. F. 17 (2)/79-Pub.-The
following Order made by the President is hereby published for general
information:-
In pursuance of the Proclamation
of the fifth day of July, 1977, read with the Laws (Continuance in Force)
Order, 1977 (C. M. L. A. Order No. I of 1977), and in exercise of all powers
enabling him in that behalf, the President and Chief Martial Law Administrator
is pleased to wake the following Order--
1. Short title, application and commencement.-(1) This Order may be
called the National and Provincial Assemblies (Basis of Elections) Order, 1979.
(2) It shall apply only in
respect of the forthcoming elections to the National Assembly and the
Provincial Assemblies.
(3) It shall come into force at
once.
2. Order to override other laws.-This Order shall have effect
notwith standing anything contained in the Constitution or in any law relating
to election to the National Assembly and the Provincial Assemblies.
3. Interpretation.-Words and expressions used in this Order shall,
unless the context otherwise requires, have the same meaning as in the
Representation of the People Act, 1976 (LXXXV of 1976).
4. Elections to be held on the basis of proportional Representation.-(1)
Elections to the Muslim seats in the National Assembly, except the seats
allocated to the Federally Administered Tribal Areas, and to the Muslim seats
in the Provincial Assemblies shall be held on the basis of proportional
representation in accordance with the provisions of this Order and law.
(2) For the purposes of elections
to the seats in the National Assembly, the Federal Capital shall be deemed to
form part of the Province of the Punjab.
(3) Nothing in this Order shall
be deemed to affect the right to be declared elected to a seat in the National
Assembly or a Provincial Assembly of a person who is the only contesting
candidate for election to such seat or who has contested election to such seat
otherwise than as the candidate or nominee of a political party, hereinafter
referred to as an independent candidate, and has secured the highest number of
votes.
5. Compilation of votes by the Commission in respect of elections.-(1)
The Commission shall compile the enumeration of votes cast for election to the
seats in the National Assembly and a Provincial Assembly received from the
Returning Officers in each Province and determine the total number of valid
votes polled by persons contesting the election as the candidates or nominees
of each political party and the independent candidates.
Explanation.-In this clause, and
in the succeeding provisions of this Order, political party means a political
party registered under the Political Parties Act, 1962 (III of 1962).
(2) The votes polled by the
persons contesting the election as the candidates or nominees of a political
party shall be deemed; for the purposes of this Order, to be votes secured by
or cast for that political party:
Provided that, in the case of a
person contesting election to more than one seat, whether in the same Assembly
or in different Assemblies, as the candidate or nominee of a political party,
only the votes polled by him in the constituency in which he had polled the
highest percentage of votes shall be deemed to be votes secured by or cast for
that political party and the votes polled by him in any other constituency
shall be treated as having been polled by an independent candidate.
6. Declaration of results by the Commission.-(1) The Commission
shall calculate the total number of valid votes secured by each political
